name.en: Fake traffic e-challan: “pending fine, pay now or licence suspended”

how.en: An SMS or WhatsApp message, often with your vehicle number, says you have an unpaid traffic challan and must pay now to avoid a court case, a higher fine or licence suspension. It contains a link to a site that copies the Parivahan e-challan portal, or an APK such as “RTO Challan” or “mParivahan”. The site steals card details and OTPs; the app takes over your phone and bank OTPs. Check challans only on the official Parivahan e-challan portal.

text.en: A message says a traffic fine on your vehicle is pending.
It threatens court, extra fines or licence suspension if not paid now.
It has a payment link or an APK file to download.
The page asks for card details, CVV or OTP.
Traffic Dept: A challan of Rs 1,000 is pending on your vehicle for over-speeding. Pay today to avoid court action and DL suspension. Pay here: [link]
RTO notice: your e-challan details are attached. Download RTO_Challan.apk to view and pay the fine.

en: traffic challan sms with payment link
pending e challan link in sms
message about traffic violations on my vehicle
challan message asked for card details
A payment link or APK in a challan message.
Threats of court or licence suspension today.
A website that isn't on a .gov.in address.
Don't tap the link or open the file.
Check your vehicle number yourself on the official Parivahan e-challan portal or your state traffic police site.
If you paid or installed something, call your bank and 1930.
